The Lagos State Police Command has said it is yet to confirm receipt of the bench warrant issued by a Lagos State High Court sitting in Ikoyi for the arrest of the Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya. The command’s Public Relations Officer disclosed this to Saturday PUNCH on Friday. Justice O. Adewunmi-Oshin issued the warrant on Thursday after Odukoya failed to appear in court in a case brought by the Incorporated Trustees of the church. The case arose from the church’s leadership crisis, with the trustees accusing Odukoya of disobeying a subsisting court order restraining him from parading himself as its Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head or interfering with its governance and activities. Justice Adewunmi-Oshin noted that Odukoya failed to obey an earlier directive requiring him to appear in court and show cause why he should not be committed to prison for allegedly disobeying a subsisting order. The court also directed that the matter be returned to the administrative judge for reassignment. At the proceedings, Odukoya’s counsel, Wale Akoni, SAN, informed the court that his client had filed a notice of appeal and an application for a stay of execution against the order directing him to appear. However, the judge held that the filing of an appeal did not excuse the pastor’s failure to comply with the court’s directive. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. When Saturday PUNCH contacted the Police Public Relations Officer of the command, Abimbola Adebisi, on Friday, an aide to the PPRO said they were yet to establish whether the police had received the court order. “I’m trying to make enquiries from our legal department. I have already reached out to the department to find out if they have received the warrant, but I have not gotten any response from them yet.” “You know this is the weekend and it is already late. And it is not something that is an emergency, so they (legal department) might not give it much attention. “However, if anything comes up, I will get back to you as soon as I get anything on it,” he said. The latest development is part of a deepening leadership crisis at the church, founded in 1992 by Odukoya’s late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, and his late wife, Bimbo. The dispute became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Jimmy was no longer recognised as senior pastor, citing a review of the church’s constitution and a video recording containing what it described as the late founder’s succession instructions. The trustees noted that the recording was not presented when Jimmy was appointed senior pastor in September 2023, following his father’s death. They subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. However, Odukoya rejected his removal, arguing that it was not based on a valid decision of the church’s recognised Board of Trustees. He maintained that his appointment in 2023 was unanimously approved and that he remained the duly appointed senior pastor. The dispute also moved to the Federal High Court in Lagos, where Odukoya and the church’s Incorporated Trustees instituted a suit challenging the validity of resolutions taken by some members of the board. The action named his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church members as defendants. The legal battle intensified after the Lagos State High Court issued its restraining order. The order was granted ex parte—meaning it was issued without first hearing Odukoya’s response—but preserved his right to apply to have it set aside or respond to the substantive claims after being served. Addressing worshippers during a church service on November 22, Odukoya said he had heard about the injunction but had not received the court documents. “I heard there was an injunction against me. I heard, but I have not seen it, and I have not been served. They said that there was no substituted service. Legally, I have not been served,” he said. He also reassured members of the congregation, saying, “You know there is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life, and as long as you would have me, I will continue to speak for you.” Olufemi Adediran
